subject: Oceanography
title: Ice Cores
description: Learn Ice Cores in one minute.

hook.text: Air bubbles trapped in Antarctic ice record Earth's atmosphere from 800,000 years ago—a frozen time capsule.

buildup.text: Each year's snowfall compresses into a layer of ice—trapping dust, volcanic ash, and tiny air bubbles.

discovery.text: Scientists drill cores up to 3 km deep—each layer reveals temperature, CO₂, and methane at that time.

twist.text: Ice cores proved that CO₂ and temperature have always risen and fallen together—tightly coupled for 800,000 years.

climax.text: Today's CO₂ level (424 ppm) is 50% higher than any point in those 800,000 years—we are in uncharted territory.

punchline.text: Ancient ice tells us where we've been—and warns where we're going.

quiz.question: How far back can ice cores record Earth's atmosphere?
